findings.issue: Hero grid tracks collapse at every width >=1024. The h1's widest line ('formata.' plus its pl-[1em] indent) gives the left track a 675.375px min-content that exceeds its 1.3fr share, and the right track is then sized intrinsically instead of taking the remaining space. Computed grid-template-columns is '675.375px 154.438px' at 1024 and '675.375px 244.031px' at 1440/1920, against a 1088px container. Three consequences: (a) the primary 'Rezervisi cas' CTA is 154px at 1024 and its label wraps to two lines - the page's most important control is visibly broken and narrower than the header's own 160px CTA sitting directly above it; (b) the lede paragraph is set in a 154px measure, four lines of two or three words; (c) 66px (1024) / 105px (1440+) of dead ink sits to the right of the whole column, so the hero's right edge (926 @1024, 1159 @1440) no longer aligns with the header CTA, the board rules or the closing CTA (all at 1264 @1440). This is newly introduced - the BEFORE shot has the hero CTA running to 1264, flush. Fix by capping the track, e.g. lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1.3fr)_minmax(18rem,0.7fr)], or by trimming the h1's last-line indent so the left track's min-content stays under its fr share.

Live Playwright measurement: getComputedStyle(heroGrid).gridTemplateColumns === '675.375px 154.438px' @1024, '675.375px 244.031px' @1440 and @1920.

findings.issue: Each of the four non-entry format rows ends its content at x=1008 while its rule runs the full container to x=1264 - a 256px empty tail per row, four rows deep - and the name-to-description gutter is still 116-220px on short names. findings.issue: The two renderings of the formats data disagree on heading semantics. The desktop board sets each format name as an <h3>, but the phone tiles set it as a plain <span> inside <summary>, and the desktop <ul> is display:none below 768 - so on a phone the five format names leave the heading outline entirely. Making the summary label an <h3> costs nothing and keeps one outline at both widths.

findings.issue: The page's one container break stops short of the viewport on wide screens. The mark's overhang is a fixed negative margin (xl:-mr-24), so it reaches the edge only at exactly 1280; at 1440 it terminates 80px inside the viewport and at 1920 320px inside, where a machine drawn with a finishing riser cap reads as a misaligned element rather than a rail continuing off the page. Since the scrollbar concern behind the declared deviation applies to calc(50% - 50vw), a viewport-unit width on the mark wrapper or a wider xl/2xl step would restore the intent.
findings.evidence: .tmp/shots-after/telo-pilates-desktop.png at 1440: the right riser stands at x=1360 with 80px of ink to its right. Live measurement: markSvg right = 1024 @1024, 1280 @1280, 1360 @1440, 1600 @1920.

overall: The structural work genuinely landed and the diagnosis behind it was accurate: the mark is now a real picture rather than a hairline squiggle, the method band's hierarchy is inverted the right way round with the apparatus at display scale and the false language-switcher gone, the ghost numerals and the chalk seam are deleted, the phone board is re-authored as native tap tiles rather than stacked, kickers are at zero, and the weight monopoly is broken. The keep-list survived intact - three-colour ink-dominant palette untouched, one type family, nothing from data.ts researchOnly rendered, method.claim still attributed, CTA discipline held, zero-JS scroll motion with the settled default and both focus-ring variants preserved, no images, no console errors, no horizontal overflow at any of 390/768/1024/1280/1440/1920. It is not yet at the level of the best four, for one reason above all: the h1 rewrite silently collapsed the hero's right grid track at every width from 1024 up, so the primary CTA is 154px with a two-line label at 1024 and the hero's right edge no longer aligns with anything else on the page - the first thing a laptop visitor sees. Close that plus the formats board's 256px-per-row tail void and this page is there.
